The PR adds inline detection for whitespace-separated leading `NO_REPLY` tokens in reply normalization and adds three regression tests.

PR surface: Source +22, Tests +30. Total +52 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. The supplied baseline proof and current-main source establish a high-confidence path where glued-leading detection fails and trailing-only cleanup leaves the prefix intact.

target.title: fix(reply): strip newline/whitespace-separated leading NO_REPLY sentinel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103735. Follow-up to #30916 and #30955.

When a model emits `NO_REPLY` on its own line before the real reply body:

```
NO_REPLY

Wait — the user mentioned me directly. I should respond.

Hi! How can I help?
```

…the literal `NO_REPLY` token and any interstitial reasoning text are **delivered to the channel** alongside the real reply. The sentinel should be stripped.

## Root Cause

`startsWithSilentToken` (`tokens.ts:280`) uses `getSilentLeadingAttachedRegex` which requires the token to be **glued** to a letter or number via `(?=[\p{L}\p{N}])`. A newline/whitespace-separated leading token is not detected, so `stripLeadingSilentToken` is never called. The `stripSilentToken` fallback only handles **trailing** tokens (`\s*$`), so the leading token survives.

The punctuation safe harbour (`NO_REPLY: explanation`, `NO_REPLY -- nope`) is preserved — a punctuation-separated token is substantive text, not a sentinel.

## Fix

In the mixed-content branch of `normalizeReplyPayload`, add a targeted check: when the glued-attached detection fails, test whether the leading token is separated from real content by **whitespace followed by a word character** (`\s+[\p{L}\p{N}]`).

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/normalize-reply.ts` | 12 lines added in mixed-content branch |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-utils.test.ts` | 3 new regression tests |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — OpenClaw main + PR patch, live Node.js import

```
$ node --import tsx/esm -e "import { normalizeReplyPayload } from './src/auto-reply/reply/normalize-reply.js'; ..."

--- Leading whitespace-separated (FIXED) ---
✅ Newline-separated:  "NO_REPLY\n\nWait..."         → "Wait..."         (token stripped)
✅ Space-separated:    "NO_REPLY  The answer is 42." → "The answer..."   (token stripped)
✅ Tab-separated:      "NO_REPLY\tThe answer..."     → "The answer..."   (token stripped)

--- Suppression when stripping leaves nothing ---
✅ Whitespace-only after strip → null (silent skip)

--- Safe harbour preserved ---
✅ Punctuation colon:  "NO_REPLY: explanation"       → preserved
✅ Punctuation dash:   "NO_REPLY—note"               → preserved
✅ Double dash:        "NO_REPLY -- nope"            → preserved

--- Existing behavior preserved ---
✅ Glued leading:      "NO_REPLYhello"               → "hello"
✅ Trailing token:     "File is there.\n\nNO_REPLY"  → "File is there."
✅ Emoji trailing:     "😄 NO_REPLY"                  → "😄"
```

### Mantis Telegram Desktop Proof

Mantis captured native Telegram Desktop before/after GIFs: the leading `NO_REPLY` preamble is removed from the final delivered message while the substantive reply content is preserved.

### Vitest

```
✓ strips newline-separated leading NO_REPLY from mixed-content text (#103735)
✓ strips leading NO_REPLY separated by spaces from content (#103735)
✓ suppresses when stripping leading NO_REPLY leaves only whitespace (#103735)
✓ strips glued leading NO_REPLY text without leaking the token
✓ strips NO_REPLY from mixed emoji message (#30916)
✓ strips NO_REPLY appended after substantive text (#30916)
✓ keeps NO_REPLY when used as leading substantive text
✓ keeps punctuation-start content after a leading NO_REPLY token
```
